newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda produces V6 engine in Ohio plant.
newsitem.headline: Honda produces V6 engine in Ohio plant.

text.p: Honda Motor Co. Ltd said Thursday it has started production of a V6 3-litre engine at its plant in Anna, Ohio.

The VTEC (Variable Valve Timing & Lift Electronic Control) engine will be installed in the automaker's new Acura 3.0CL luxury two-door coupe. Honda will start producing the coupe at its East Liberty, Ohio, plant on Sept. 10.
The engine will be also used in Honda's new Minivan, which will be produced from the fall of 1998 at Honda of Canada Mfg. Inc. in Alliston, Ontario.
Honda spent $200 million for new production facilities to produce the V6 engine and an in-line 2.2-litre 4-cylinder engine at the Anna plant.
This plant is now the largest single source of engines in the world for Honda, with a capacity of 900,000 engines a year. Initially, V6 engine production will be about 100 a day.
The new line will lead to the hiring of 200 additional workers at the Anna plant by 1998, adding to the current 2,300 employees.
The plant now produces 1.6- and 2.2-litre car engines and 1.52-litre motorcycle engines. The plant produced 605,127 engines in 1995 and is expected to produce 650,000 in 1996.
